name: listAllowedDirectories
description: Reports which directories the filesystem tools may touch: the readable roots (your home directory and the app's spring-ai-playground folder - anything under them can be read) and the single working directory for this chat (the only writable location, where relative paths resolve). Files the user uploads are saved under the working directory's uploads/ subfolder, so after calling this you can listDir the working directory or its uploads/ folder to see the files already there, then readTextFile one to re-process it. Call this first to learn the absolute paths. Takes no arguments. Uses safety.fs.readRoots()/workspace().

name: readTextFile
description:
Reads a UTF-8 text file from disk and returns its full contents as a string. Works on any text file — Markdown, JSON, CSV, source code, .txt, and so on (not binary); choose which file with `path`.

A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path is allowed anywhere under a readable root (the user's home directory by default). Call listAllowedDirectories first to learn the working directory and readable roots. Uses safety.fs.readText().

params.name: path
params.description: The file to read, INCLUDING its extension — e.g. `README.md`, `package.json`, or an absolute path like `/Users/you/Documents/report.md`. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

code:
/**
 * Reads a UTF-8 text file inside the playground's FS base directory.
 *
 * Path is resolved RELATIVE to the base path (which is set via
 * `spring.ai.playground.tool-studio.fs.base-path`,
 * defaulting to the user's home directory). Anything attempting
 * to escape the base (e.g. `../`) is rejected by safety.fs.
 *
 * Uses host helper: safety.fs.readText.
 */

if (path == null || path === '') throw new Error('path required');
return safety.fs.readText(path);

name: listDir
description: Lists the immediate entries (files and subdirectories) of a directory. Entries inside the working directory are returned as relative names; entries elsewhere under a readable root are returned as absolute paths. Pass '.' for the working directory, or an absolute path for any readable root (call listAllowedDirectories). Uses safety.fs.list().

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory to list. Relative (default '.') resolves under the working directory; an absolute path under a readable root is also allowed.

name: statFile
description: Returns size, last-modified timestamp, and a directory flag for a path. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories). Uses safety.fs.stat().

params.name: path
params.description: Path to read. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

code:
/**
 * Returns { size, mtime, directory } for a path inside the FS base.
 *
 * - size       — file size in bytes (0 for directories).
 * - mtime      — ISO timestamp of last modification.
 * - directory  — true if the path is a directory.
 *
 * Uses host helper: safety.fs.stat.
 */

if (path == null || path === '') throw new Error('path required');
return safety.fs.stat(path);

name: lineCount
description: Counts the lines in a UTF-8 text file. Uses safety.fs.lineCount().

params.name: path
params.description: Path to the file. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

name: sliceFile
description: Returns a slice of lines from a UTF-8 text file (head / tail / range). `start` is 0-based inclusive, `end` is 0-based exclusive (Python-style slice). Negative values count from the end of the file. Uses safety.fs.slice().

params.name: path
params.description: Path to the file. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

params.name: start
params.description: First line index (0-based inclusive; negatives from end)

params.name: end
params.description: End line index (0-based exclusive; negatives from end)

code:
/**
 * Returns lines [start, end) from a UTF-8 text file (Python-slice semantics).
 *
 * - `start` is 0-based and inclusive.
 * - `end`   is 0-based and exclusive.
 * - Negative values count from the end: -1 == size - 1.
 * - Missing `start` / `end` defaults to the file's full range.
 *
 * Uses host helper: safety.fs.slice.
 */

if (path == null || path === '') throw new Error('path required');
return safety.fs.slice(path, start, end);

name: sortFile
description: Sorts the lines of a UTF-8 text file and returns the sorted lines as an array. Options: reverse / numeric / caseInsensitive / unique. Uses safety.fs.sort().

params.name: path
params.description: Path to the file. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

params.name: reverse
params.description: Sort descending

params.name: numeric
params.description: Sort lines numerically

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.description: Ignore case when comparing

params.name: unique
params.description: Drop duplicate lines

code:
/**
 * Sorts a file's lines and returns them as an array.
 *
 * Options:
 *   reverse           — descending order
 *   numeric           — numeric comparison (otherwise lexical)
 *   caseInsensitive   — compare lowercased
 *   unique            — drop duplicates
 *
 * Uses host helper: safety.fs.sort.
 */

if (path == null || path === '') throw new Error('path required');
return safety.fs.sort(path, {
  reverse: !!reverse,
  numeric: !!numeric,
  caseInsensitive: !!caseInsensitive,
  unique: !!unique,
});

name: grepFile
description: Searches a UTF-8 text file for lines matching a JavaScript regex. Returns an array of matching lines (optionally numbered). Uses safety.fs.grep().

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regex pattern (JavaScript flavour)

params.name: path
params.description: Path to the file. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.description: Match case-insensitively

params.name: numbered
params.description: Prefix each result with 'N:' (1-based line number)

params.name: limit
params.description: Max matches to return (0 = no limit)

name: findFiles
description: Recursively finds files matching a glob inside a directory. Glob supports `*` and `?`. Optional max recursion depth and type filter ('file' or 'dir'). Uses safety.fs.find().

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory to search from. Relative (default '.') resolves under the working directory; an absolute path under a readable root is also allowed.

params.name: glob
params.description: Glob pattern (default '*')

params.name: maxDepth
params.description: Max recursion depth (0 = unlimited)

params.name: type
params.description: 'file' | 'dir' | omit for both

name: cutFileFields
description: Extracts selected fields from each line of a delimited file (CSV/TSV/etc.). Uses safety.fs.cut(). 1-based field numbers, comma-separated alternatives via the array.

params.name: path
params.description: Path to the file. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

params.name: fields
params.description: Array of 1-based field indices to keep, e.g. [1, 3]

params.name: delimiter
params.description: Field delimiter character or regex (default '\t' tab)

params.name: regex
params.description: Treat `delimiter` as a regex pattern instead of literal

name: writeTextFile
description: Use this to save a file to disk. Writes the text `content` to the file named by `path`, and returns where it was written. You pick the filename and extension on every call, so this creates ANY UTF-8 text file — Markdown (.md), JSON, CSV, source code, HTML, plain .txt, and so on (it cannot write binary such as images). Parent directories are created automatically and an existing file is overwritten. Writes are confined to the working directory: a relative path lands there, and any path that resolves outside it (absolute paths or `../`) is rejected — call listAllowedDirectories to see the working directory. Returns { ok, path, bytes }, where `path` is the absolute location actually written. Requires `fileWrite` permission on the sandbox.

params.name: path
params.description: Where to save it, INCLUDING the filename and the extension you want — e.g. `report.md`, `data.json`, `src/app.py`, `notes.txt`. Pick this per call. A relative path resolves inside the working directory (the only writable location); absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

params.name: content
params.description: The complete text to write (UTF-8), in whatever format matches the extension in `path` — Markdown, JSON, CSV, source code, plain text, etc. Written verbatim, so pass the full, final file body.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to write to a file. Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: searchInFiles
description: Searches file CONTENTS across a directory tree for lines matching a JavaScript regex, returning every hit as { file, line, text }. This is recursive multi-file search: unlike grepFile (one file) or findFiles (matches file NAMES only), this opens each file under `dir` whose name matches `glob` and scans its lines. Use it to answer 'which files mention X' or 'where is Y used'. A relative `dir` resolves under the working directory; an absolute `dir` must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories). Binary/non-UTF-8 files are skipped. Uses safety.fs.searchInFiles().

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regex pattern (JavaScript flavour) matched against each line's content

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory to search from. Relative (default '.') resolves under the working directory; an absolute path under a readable root is also allowed.

params.name: glob
params.description: Filename glob to limit which files are scanned (default '*'). Supports `*` and `?`.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.description: Match case-insensitively

params.name: maxDepth
params.description: Max recursion depth (0 = unlimited)

params.name: limit
params.description: Max total matches to return (0 = default cap)

name: appendTextFile
description: Appends UTF-8 text to the END of a file, creating it if it does not exist. Unlike writeTextFile (which overwrites the whole file), this adds `content` after the existing bytes, so it is ideal for logs, incremental output, and streaming results. Writes are confined to the working directory: a relative path lands there, and any path that resolves outside it (absolute or `../`) is rejected. Returns { ok, path, bytesAppended }. Uses safety.fs.appendText().

params.name: path
params.description: File to append to, INCLUDING the filename and extension. A relative path resolves inside the working directory (the only writable location); absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

params.name: content
params.description: The UTF-8 text to append verbatim after the existing content.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to append to a file. Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: editTextFile
description: Makes a targeted edit to an existing text file by replacing an exact substring, WITHOUT rewriting the whole file. Give the exact `oldString` to find and the `newString` to put in its place. By default `oldString` must occur EXACTLY ONCE (otherwise the call is rejected as ambiguous, so include enough surrounding context to make it unique); set replaceAll=true to replace every occurrence. Use this instead of writeTextFile whenever you only need to change part of a file. Writes are confined to the working directory. Returns { ok, path, replacements }. Uses safety.fs.editText().

params.name: path
params.description: File to edit, INCLUDING the filename and extension. A relative path resolves inside the working directory (the only writable location); absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

params.name: oldString
params.description: The exact text to find. Must match verbatim (including whitespace). Unless replaceAll is true it must occur exactly once, so include surrounding context to make it unique.

params.name: newString
params.description: The replacement text. Pass an empty string to delete the matched text.

params.name: replaceAll
params.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a single unique match

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to edit a file. Allow '{toolName}' on {args}?

name: copyFile
description: Copies a file to a new location. The source may be any readable file (under a readable root such as your home directory, or an uploaded file in the working directory); the destination must be inside the working directory (the only writable location). Parent directories are created automatically and an existing destination is overwritten. The source is left untouched. Returns { ok, path } where `path` is where the copy was written. Uses safety.fs.copy().

params.name: from
params.description: Source file to copy. A relative path resolves under the working directory; an absolute path must sit under a readable root (call listAllowedDirectories).

params.name: to
params.description: Destination path, INCLUDING the filename. Must resolve inside the working directory; absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to copy a file (this may overwrite the destination). Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: moveFile
description: Moves or renames a file within the working directory. Both the source and destination must be inside the working directory (the only writable location). Parent directories are created automatically and an existing destination is overwritten. This is destructive: the source no longer exists at its old path afterwards, and it cannot be undone. Returns { ok, path } where `path` is the new location. Uses safety.fs.move().

params.name: from
params.description: Source file to move. Must resolve inside the working directory; absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

params.name: to
params.description: Destination path, INCLUDING the new filename. Must resolve inside the working directory.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to move/rename a file (this may overwrite the destination, and the source is removed). Allow '{toolName}' with {args}?

name: deleteFile
description: Permanently deletes a single file from the working directory (the only writable location). This is destructive and cannot be undone. Directories are rejected: use deleteDir for those. Returns { ok, deleted, path } where `deleted` is true if a file was removed (false if it did not exist). Uses safety.fs.delete().

params.name: path
params.description: File to delete. Must resolve inside the working directory; absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to DELETE a file. Allow '{toolName}' to remove {args}? This cannot be undone.

name: deleteDir
description: Permanently deletes a directory AND ALL of its contents (recursive) from the working directory (the only writable location). This is destructive and cannot be undone. The working directory root itself cannot be deleted, and plain files are rejected (use deleteFile). Returns { ok, removed, path } where `removed` is the number of entries deleted. Uses safety.fs.deleteDir().

params.name: path
params.description: Directory to delete recursively. Must resolve inside the working directory (and cannot be the working directory root); absolute paths and `../` escapes are rejected.

humanInTheLoop.promptTemplate: The assistant wants to DELETE a directory and ALL its contents (recursive). Allow '{toolName}' on {args}? This cannot be undone.
